title: How to use a word for public policy advocates on Mac: efficiency guide
metaTitle: Word for public policy advocates on Mac: efficiency tips and Lazur
description: Improve your document workflow in Microsoft Word for Mac. Learn essential shortcuts and how to use Lazur to save time on policy briefs and reports.
targetKeyword: word for public policy advocates on mac
intro: Public policy advocates on Mac need a reliable way to manage high volumes of legislative text and complex briefs. Using Microsoft Word for Mac effectively requires mastering specific keyboard shortcuts and automating repetitive formatting tasks to maintain your focus on advocacy work.
tldr: Master keyboard shortcuts like ⌘ + ⌥ + V to paste without formatting.
Use styles to ensure consistent document structure across long policy reports.
Leverage Lazur to dictate notes and ask for help with complex Word menus.
Keep your system updated to version 16.114.1 for the best stability.
Use ⌥ + ⌘ to ask Lazur for help with specific ribbon locations.

stats.label: Average workweek time spent on email tasks

blocks.text: Efficiency starts with your keyboard. Stop relying on your mouse to navigate the ribbon. Use ⌘ + ⌥ + Arrow Keys to move through your document by word. Use ⌘ + Arrow Keys to jump to the start or end of a line. These small movements add up during a long day of drafting policy memos.

Consistency is key when you present data to policymakers. Use the Styles pane to manage your headings. Open it with ⌥ + ⌘ + S. This allows you to update the font or size of every Heading 1 in your document at once. It prevents the common mistake of manual formatting that breaks when you export to PDF.

items: Use ⌘ + ⇧ + V to paste text without keeping the source formatting.
Use ⌘ + ⌥ + 1 to quickly apply the Heading 1 style.
Press ⌃ + ⌘ + Space to open the character viewer for special symbols.
Use ⌘ + K to insert a link to your source material.

blocks.text: Using Lazur to speed up your drafting

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you stay in the flow. Hold the fn key to dictate your thoughts directly into Word. This is useful for getting a first draft of a talking point onto the page before you refine it. If you forget where a specific setting is, hold ⌥ + ⌘ and ask Lazur. It will circle the button on your screen.

Policy documents often grow to dozens of pages. Use [insert a section break in Word](/how-to/insert-a-section-break-in-word) to manage headers and footers effectively. If you need a table of contents, ensure you have used proper heading styles first. Then use [insert a table of contents in Word](/how-to/insert-a-table-of-contents-in-word) to generate it automatically.

Many advocates struggle with file compatibility between Windows and Mac. If your document looks different on a colleague's machine, check your font settings. Always save your final drafts as PDF to ensure the layout remains identical. If Word crashes, check your AutoRecover folder. Use [recover an unsaved document in Word](/how-to/recover-an-unsaved-document-in-word) to find your work.
How to stay organized with your advocacy work

Use [create a template in Word](/how-to/create-a-template-in-word) for your recurring policy briefs. This saves time on layout and branding for every new project. Store these in a dedicated folder on your Mac. Combine this with consistent naming conventions to keep your research accessible.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Microsoft Word for Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur runs on your Mac and can see your screen while Word is open. You can ask it to explain features, point at tools, or dictate text into your document.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to edit my Word files?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files for you. It helps you by pointing out where tools are or by dictating text at your cursor.

faq.question: What is the best way to move between windows in Word?
faq.answer: Use ⌘ + ` to cycle through open Word documents on your Mac.
